newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ELECTRICITY EASES WITH CASH, POWER SUPPLY.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ELECTRICITY EASES WITH CASH, POWER SUPPLY.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures eased Tuesday with lower physical prices and healthy power generation through the West, industry sources said.

As of 1220 EDT, September Palo Verde (PV) was down $1.06 at the day's low of $30.75 per megawatt hour (MWh) following trade as high as $31.30, while October was down 55 cents at the day's high of $23.75 after reaching as low as $23.60 per MWh.
September California Oregon Border (COB) was down 55 cents at the day's low of $23.05 after hitting a high of $23.30, while October was down 31 cents at $22.70 per MWh.
NYMEX said that as of 1140 EDT an estimated total of 190 PV and 49 COB contracts had traded.
In the physical markets, next-day peak power at PV was said to be trading near $36.00 from $40.00-44.00 Monday, while next-day peak COB was said to be trading near $22.00 from $20.50-23.00 Monday.
"We have pretty good generation overall in the West right now, a lot of units that had been having problems are back," said one electricity futures trader.
In generation news, the 670 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Centralia coal-fired power station in Washington state was tentatively set to shut Monday for a two-day outage.
A 700 MW unit at the Colstrip coal-fired power plant in Montana was heard shut last Friday for repairs, and expected to resume operations today.

The 750 MW unit 3 at the Navajo coal-fired power station near Page, Ariz., was scheduled to restart Monday afternoon after being shut over the weekend for repairs. Navajo's other two 750 MW units were said to be operating normally.

Separately, southbound transmission capacity on the Pacific Intertie will be cut by 350 MW to 850 MW during certain hours on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday of this week, according to the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA).

Forecasters said scattered showers and thunderstorms were expected to keep temperatures cool in the northeastern part of the Southwest. Readings for the rest of the region would run normal to slightly above normal.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to average below normal across most of the region with the exception of the far west area which would run slightly above than normal.
